result.summary:
I ported npm diff@8.0.4 (jsdiff) to `pi_js::vendor::jsdiff` and synced it. It includes the seven required functions — diff_lines, diff_words, structured_patch, create_two_files_patch, create_patch, apply_patch, parse_patch — and the rest of the public surface except diffJson, jsonDiff and canonicalize.

The parity tests pass: 10 tests over about 3,600 vectors generated from the real library, plus two larger throwaway stress runs that also matched. Check, clippy and rustfmt were clean for my files.

**One blocker:** pi-js will not compile in the main tree until pijs-core lands `pi_js::error` and `pi_js::time` (both are still 1-line stubs). I tested against temporary stand-ins for those two files in the clone and restored the original stubs before syncing.

What the port covers:
- **Diffing:** every jsdiff diff kind and option, including maxEditLength/timeout and a callback that replaces Intl.Segmenter. The Myers algorithm is ported directly.
- **Patches:** create, format, parse (same error messages as jsdiff), reverse, line-ending conversion, `apply_patch` (fuzz, offsets, end-of-file newline handling, CRLF auto-conversion, custom line comparison) and `apply_patches`.
- **Converters:** convert_changes_to_dmp and convert_changes_to_xml.

API differences from the JS library:
- Each function that can abort has a separate `*_abortable` variant that returns `None` where JS returns `undefined`.
- `apply_patch` returns `Ok(None)` where JS returns `false`.
- Functions that also take an array of patches have an `*_array` variant.

All other differences are listed in gaps_remaining with their `// PORT:` locations.

The sync copied 26 files with no conflicts or rejections. The clone and the /tmp scratch files have been removed.

result.summary:
I found no parity bugs in the jsdiff port, so no source file changed; the only synced file is a new test. It cannot compile in the main tree yet, because the pi_js error and time modules it uses are still 1-line stubs owned by pijs-core. I tested in the clone with temporary shims for those two modules (reverted, not synced).

**Contract check.** Every Appendix A function exists as snake(jsdiff export): diff_lines, diff_words, structured_patch, create_two_files_patch, create_patch, apply_patch, parse_patch. Most other diff@8.0.4 exports are also ported. That includes the other diff_* functions, the format/reverse patch functions, apply_patches, the header constants, the line-ending helpers and the converters. `*_abortable` variants return None where JS returns undefined.

**Code paths pi relies on.** pi calls `Diff.diffLines(old, new)` and `Diff.createTwoFilesPatch(path, path, old, new, undefined, undefined, {context, headerOptions: FILE_HEADERS_ONLY})` in the edit-diff files. It calls `Diff.diffWords(old, new)` in the interactive diff component, and `applyPatch(source, patch)` in two test files. I compared each against node_modules/diff/libesm line by line and found no behaviour difference. Areas covered:
- the Myers search (bestPath and diagonal pruning, maxEditLength/timeout checks)
- extractCommon and addToPath with oneChangePerToken
- the word tokenizer regexes with the JS whitespace set and extended word characters
- the whitespace clean-up after diffWords and its string helpers
- the line tokenizer (`split(/(\n|\r\n)/)`) and its equals options
- splitLines, context slicing (negative, fractional, NaN, Infinity), and the "\ No newline at end of file" handling in patch creation
- apply: EOF-newline handling, fuzz recursion, `lines[toPos]` returning undefined, joining undefined lines, error message texts
- parsePatch: regexes, quoted names, `split('\t', 2)`, NaN headers, count checks and their messages
- line-ending conversion and the distance iterator

**JS-semantics check.** UTF-16 vs char differences only affect the internal string helpers on split surrogate pairs, and diffWords only calls those on whitespace. Hunk header numbers use ryu-js. JSON.stringify of strings in error messages matches serde_json's escaping. A grep found no placeholders (the one TODO is a comment copied from jsdiff).

**Test added.** `pijs_jsdiff_differential.rs` holds 1430 vectors generated from the real library, aimed at pi's call shapes, plus two tests whose expected values I checked in Node. The remaining deviations (diffJson not ported, async callback option, formatPatch not mutating its input, panic instead of throw) are listed in gaps_remaining.

fs.watch (needs notify, which only pi-coding-agent depends on) and globSync are not in pi_js::fs. Their coding-agent callers must provide them.
createWriteStream/createReadStream are not ported. Callers can use fs::open + File::write_all/read (sync File and promises FileHandle are provided).

Windows paths are unverified (no Windows target installed): Win32-to-uv error mapping, the Stats mode synthesis, EISDIR on open of a directory, symlink file/dir detection, and the rmSync C++ errno values (1/41/20, EIO for access denied).
rmSync recursive error text after a partial failure follows the toolchain's std::filesystem: macOS libc++ is node-verified; the Linux libstdc++ first-error behaviour is approximated and untested.

PORT deviations: set_interval delivers missed ticks in a burst (tokio Burst, matches vitest fake timers rather than Node's reschedule-from-callback). iso_string returns 'Invalid Date' instead of throwing (try_iso_string returns the RangeError). env::cwd falls back to $PWD or / when getcwd fails (Node throws). watch_file polls separately per call (Node shares one poller per path). The set_timeout/set_interval no-runtime fallback uses std::thread::sleep. os_release/os_version on Windows parse `cmd /c ver` instead of RtlGetVersion. performance_now can be negative when a paused test clock is behind the first call.

result.summary:
Parity review of pijs-system is done and synced. All 8 owned files are identical in the main tree. In the clone, cargo check, clippy for my files, rustfmt, the §13.3 lint gates and all 49 tests were clean or passing. They ran against temporary error.rs/abort.rs shims that I restored before sync. Main does not compile until pijs-core lands, so nothing has been run against the real error and abort modules.

What this pass did:
- **fs.rs (written from scratch):** a full node:fs port with Node's exact error text:
  - libuv error names, errno values and descriptions for unix and Windows.
  - util.inspect-based null-byte TypeErrors with the right argument name per function, and invalid-flag errors.
  - Sync and promises APIs, Stats/Dirent, a sync File and a promises FileHandle.
  - Ports of Node's recursive mkdir, rmSync (lstat check plus the C++ removal errors), promises rm (Node's bundled rimraf), the JS realpathSync walk, native realpath, and mkdtemp with sync vs promises error paths.
  - Relative paths respect CwdGuard.
  - I added watch_file (Node's fs.watchFile semantics, checked against node).
  - FileHandle calls after close now match Node's 'file closed' EBADF errors.
  - The rmSync C++ errno values for Windows were corrected.
- **time.rs, real bug fixed:** Date.parse picked the wrong UTC offset for local times right at a DST fall-back. Example: New York "2020-11-01T02:00" came out an hour early. chrono reports the transition instant as ambiguous, so candidate offsets are now round-trip validated before applying V8's earlier-offset rule. It now matches node in three zones.
- **time.rs, smaller changes:** performance_now no longer uses std::time::Instant (banned by PORTING.md).
- **env.rs:** a doc comment matched the set_var lint-gate regex and was reworded.
- **path.rs:** clippy cleanups only.

Remaining gaps are listed separately. The main ones: the pijs-core dependency; fs.watch, globSync and the stream APIs are not ported; and the Windows code paths have never been compiled or run (no Windows target installed). All /tmp scratch files are deleted.
